findings.statement: Summing component counts directly over REL_INC or TOPO_RPAR classes before ZOE classification is Q-V inexact on every demanding carrier tested.

REL_INC/TOPO_RPAR scalar-exactness in the earlier quadratic experiments does not make them whole component identities: those experiments retained exact component identity in the affine/base coordinate and compressed only interaction terms.
The first aggregation collisions repeatedly merge exact component types with the same frontier-relative incidence pattern but different support height / remaining local capacity.

The independently established CAP6_REL_INC result, which recovered the complete observed quadratic structural interaction span on the earlier demanding carriers, supplies a pre-existing structural reason to test capacity-augmented REL_INC identities.

interpretation_guard: This rejects direct descriptor aggregation as a complete component identity; it does not reject REL_INC or TOPO_RPAR as interaction coordinates.
Failure witnesses may motivate structural candidates, but the next capacity ladder must be frozen before qualification.
No absolute board elevation is reintroduced merely because frontier-relative incidence alone is insufficient as whole identity.
next_question: What is the coarsest capacity grade that, when paired with REL_INC before ZOE aggregation, preserves Q-V across the demanding carriers?
